primed_to_perform.title: Primed To Perform
primed_to_perform.text:
Skip to content
Primed To Perform
Primed to Perform Checklist
Purpose:
Clear your lens.
Neutralise fear, greed, and unrealistic expectations so you can interpret the market objectively and stick to your trading plan—regardless of the outcome.
This is what creates true winning:
Sticking to high-quality decisions, not chasing all-positive outcomes.
 At Least 30 Minutes Before Your Trading Session
Review Your Trading Plan
Refresh your edge, rules, and execution criteria.
Anchor your mind in process, not outcome.
Build Your Daily Watchlist
Tag relevant pairs on TradingView that meet your setup criteria.
Refine your focus—quality > quantity.
Forecast Your Daily Opportunities
Mentally rehearse potential setups based on your plan.
Draw key levels, scenarios, and game plans on the chart.
 15 Minutes Before Your Trading Session
10-Minute Guided Meditation
Use Headspace or your preferred app.
Drop into presence and calm your nervous system.
5-Minute 1:1 Breathing Exercise
(Inhale 5 – Hold 5 – Exhale 5 – Hold 5 — Repeat)
Balance your breath = Balance your mind
 Before Every Trading Decision
(Entry, stop-loss adjustment, take profit, etc.)
Complete the Bulletproof Your Trading Mindset Tool (v2.0)
Ground your psychology before you: 1. Enter the trade 2. Adjust your stop-loss 3. Lock in profits.
[Watch The Bulletproof Your Mindset Tool 2.0]
[Direct Access to The Bulletproof Your Mindset Tool 2.0]
Visualise Both Outcomes
Imagine the trade hitting stop-loss → unfazed.
Imagine the trade hitting take-profit → still unfazed.
Anchor your identity to execution of your process, not result of the outcome.
[Guided Visualisation – 06:20 to 08:20]
When this becomes habit, you stop reacting and start executing.
You shift from emotional trader → elite operator.
Now go prime your mind—and perform.

detach_reset.title: Detach & Reset Protocol
detach_reset.text:
Skip to content
Detach & Reset Protocol
 I’ve just taken a Loss 
After a Loss: Extract the Benefits
Powerful Reframe Question:
What are the benefits of losing a painful trade, losing money or percentage, or even losing a funded account or challenge?
Losing can feel confronting—but when viewed through the right lens, it becomes a moment of clarity, growth, and recalibration.
Core Benefits of Losing a Trade or Account
Long-Term Perspective: Losing helps you focus on consistent profitability rather than chasing short-term gains.
Motivation for Goals: It drives you to set and pursue important, clear, achievable trading goals.
Patience: Losing teaches you to wait for the right opportunities, as successful trading often requires patience.
Need for a Trading System: It underscores the importance of a well-defined trading system to avoid impulsive decisions and significant losses.
Humility and Market Awareness: Losing keeps you humble and reminds you of the market's unpredictable nature.
Resilience: It helps build resilience, thickening your skin, which is crucial in all aspects of life.
Adaptability: If losses are frequent or unnecessary, they push you to evolve—refining your strategy, mindset, and execution.
Reflection and Improvement: Prompts reflection on trading decisions, helping you understand strengths and areas for improvement.
Financial Discipline: Losing reminds you to respect risk, protect capital, and stay in the game long enough to see long-term success.
Innovation: When repeated losses occur, they often lead you to explore new tools, methods, or systems to improve your performance.
Mental Toughness: Builds mental toughness, enabling you to stay resilient during periods of market volatility or personal challenges.
Accountability: Increases accountability to stick to high-quality setups in your trading plan.
Teachable Moments: Makes you more open and teachable, encouraging continuous learning and development.
Psychological & Strategic Rewards:
Forces you to reconnect with your process and stop relying on luck or outcome.
Exposes flaws in your preparation, edge, or execution that winning often masks.
Builds emotional resilience → a vital trait for scaling capital in the long run.
Strengthens detachment from the outcome of the individual trade → reinforces your identity as a process-based trader.
Identity-Level Shifts:
Deepens humility—a trait every truly great trader embodies.
Forces you: To detach your worth from the outcome of one trade or one trading account.
Long-Term Edge:
Increases your ability to handle larger stakes without emotional collapse.
Makes your eventual success earned, not given—and that makes it sustainable.
Reprioritisation & Refocus
Gets you back to what actually matters:
Sticking to the plan
Letting the edge play out
Controlling the controllables (your perceptions, your decisions, your actions—NOT the market’s outcome or movement)
Shifts your focus from the short-term win to the long-term mission.
Emotional Resilience & Identity Growth
Increases your tolerance for emotional discomfort—key for long-term growth.
Makes you realise: “I can take a hit and still show up the next day.”
Rebuilds your identity not as a “winner” or “loser,” but as a committed professional.
Humility & Detachment Training
Knocks you out of any state of pride or overconfidence you were building.
Forces you to reconnect with process-based thinking.
Builds emotional detachment from wins and losses—the foundation of elite performance.
Strategic Refinement
Reveals weak spots in your trading plan or risk management that went unnoticed.
Makes you sharpen your preparation, journaling, and checklist usage.
Encourages you to tighten your edge and stop cutting corners.
You now have real data to refine from—not theoretical guesses.
Psychological Clarity & Self-Awareness
Forces you to reflect deeply on your mindset, emotional state, and execution.
Exposes your unconscious biases—like hidden greed, unrealistic expectations, or pride.
Teaches you to detach your identity from the outcome of a single trade.
Final Reflection
The best traders I know welcome the occasional loss—because it reminds them of the market’s inherent risk, its unpredictability, and the critical importance of staying disciplined to their trading plan and systems.
Losses are not obstacles—they’re invitations.
Every loss trains you in emotional regulation, discipline, and detachment.
Where in life will you only experience “wins”? Certainly not in your relationships, health, business, or finances.
Setbacks are life’s way of initiating you into self-mastery.
The market is your training ground.
 I’ve just taken a Win
After a Win: Extract the Hidden Risks
Powerful Reframe Question:
What are the drawbacks of winning a profitable trade, passing a funded challenge, or receiving a payout from a funded account?
Winning often feels like the reward we’re after—but left unchecked, it can quietly sabotage consistency, discipline, and emotional clarity.
Core Drawbacks of Winning a Trade or Account
False Sense of Security
Winning can lull you into complacency, reducing your awareness of risk and market volatility—lowering the value of sticking to your trading plan.
Complacency
Success can lead to skipping steps in your routine, lowering standards of trades, and assuming results will continue without effort.
Short-Term Thinking
A win can shift your focus to immediate gains and distract from your long-term trading vision.
Overconfidence
Inflated self-belief may cause you to ignore signals, take impulsive trades outside of your plan, or increase size irresponsibly.
Distraction from Your Strategy
You may chase the next win instead of sticking to the system that generated the last one.
Unrealistic Expectations
Wins create fantasies of fast success, forgetting that losses are part of any true edge.
Emotional Elation
Winning can create a state of emotional high that leads to forcing trades or overtrading.
Increased Pressure
After a funded challenge or payout, pressure to "not mess it up" can cause fear-based hesitation.
The Pedestal Trap
Placing the win on a pedestal can lead to self minimisation and anxiety when facing the next trade.
Poor Decision-Making
Emotional highs distort risk perception and reduce your ability to make clear, process-driven decisions.
Psychological Risks
Reinforces emotional bias: “That setup worked, so I must be right.”
Inflates pride and self-exaggeration, pulling you out of emotional equilibrium.
Distracts from refining/ sticking to your edge because the win feels like validation.
Builds emotional dependence on outcomes, increasing pain after the next inevitable/ unavoidable loss.
Execution Dangers
You start seeing yourself as the outlier—not the statistic (self exaggeration).
Begin skipping steps, cutting corners, or ignoring your trading plan.
Chase the high of winning, projecting unrealistic expectations onto future trades.
Strategic Pitfalls
If the win was off-plan, it reinforces gambling behaviour rather than process-based discipline.
Increased sensitivity to loss—now you’re playing to protect what you’ve gained, rather than sticking to your process. In trading 1 step back is necessary to take 3 steps forward.
Loss of patience—trying to force new trades to repeat the “rush”/ “high” of winning.
“False winning (making money on the individual trade) is the most dangerous drug in trading—because it feels like progress, but it’s sabotage in disguise.”
The Hidden Losses of Winning
1. Inflated Ego → Emotional Bias
Win = “I’m good” → Overconfidence.
Attach self-worth to outcome, not process.
Pride clouds judgment → You start seeing what you want to see.
“False winning is when the trade was profitable, but your psychology degraded.”
2. Breakdown of Discipline
Skipping the checklist, rushing into trades.
Neglecting the routines that led to the win in the first place.
Brain starts linking success with impulse—not structure.
3. Emotional Recalibration to Greed
Nervous system gets addicted to the high.
Cannot appreciate the true boring process that is necessary for consistent profitability.
Projects unrealistic expectations onto the next few trades.
Leads to FOMO, overtrading, and needing to “keep the streak alive.”
4. Risk Distortion
Underestimate risk, overestimate edge.
Emotional confidence replaces logical evaluation.
Start increasing risk size impulsively.
Start taking trades that aren’t part of your edge/ circle of competence.
5. Reinforcing Faulty Thinking
If you broke rules and still won, your brain anchors the wrong habit.
Builds a short-term edge that’s guaranteed to fail long-term.
Now you think: “I can get away with it.”
6. Dopamine Dependency
Winning taps into the same addictive circuits as gambling.
Identity starts shifting from: “I’m process-driven” → “I only matter when I win.”
You’ve entered the boom-bust emotional loop.
7. Amplifies the Pain of the Next Loss
The next loss doesn’t just sting—it feels identity-threatening.
Leads to hesitation (FOGI), revenge trading, spirals of self-doubt, or account blow-up.
Final Reflection
A win can be dangerous—if it pulls you off your process.
The greatest traders stay humble in success and composed in failure.
They know: True winning isn’t making money—it’s sticking to the plan.
The win isn't a green light to get reckless.
It's a reminder to double down on what actually works:
Process. Preparation. Patience.
 I’ve just missed a Profitable Trade
After a Missed Trade: Extract the Benefits
Powerful Reframe Question:
What are the benefits of missing a profitable trade, missing a setup that would’ve passed a funded challenge, or missing an account-growing opportunity?
Missing a high-quality trade can sting—but when seen through the lens of process, it becomes an invaluable opportunity to upgrade your awareness, discipline, and edge.
Core Benefits of Missing a Trade or Account-Passing Setup
Process Over Outcome
Missing a win challenges you to realign with your true north: process-based trading over outcome-based emotions.
Emotional Regulation
You learn how to hold emotional tension without needing to "do something"—a powerful performance skill.
Encourages Reflection
Prompts deep introspection: Was I out of alignment? Did I hesitate? Was I prepared? You begin to coach yourself.
Strengthens Resilience
Builds the emotional muscles required to stay the course, through discomfort, and show up the next day.
Enhances Learning
Missing a trade often teaches more than winning one—especially if you take time to unpack why it happened.
Maintains Long-Term Perspective
Reminds you that no single trade makes or breaks your edge—your job is to show up for the next 100.
Prevents Complacency
Keeps you alert, focused, and committed to showing up sharp every session.
Psychological Breakthroughs
Highlights any lingering outcome attachment you may be holding.
Reveals where you may be chasing milestones rather than following process.
Builds your ability to stay grounded and poised, even without external rewards.
Emotional Detachment Training
Helps you realise: “Missing a trade doesn’t mean I’ve failed.”
Strengthens your identity as a stable, process-focused trader.
Builds emotional neutrality—a requirement for elite execution.
Strategic Clarity
Brings awareness to why you missed the setup—was it hesitation, lack of clarity, or poor prep?
Surfaces blind spots in your process that otherwise go unnoticed.
Reinforces the truth: One trade doesn’t matter—your sample space does.
The Benefits of Missing a Profitable Trade
1. Builds Mental Fortitude & Detachment
Teaches you how to sit with discomfort—without reacting.
Helps you let go of “what could’ve been” and refocus on what still can be.
Strengthens your identity as someone who responds with discipline, not emotion.
2. Sharpens Self-Awareness
Encourages key questions:
“Why did I hesitate?”
“Was I mentally prepared?”
“Did I skip steps or misread the market?”
Every missed trade becomes a mirror for your mindset and your system.
3. Reveals Hidden Gaps in Process
Often missed trades surface:
Gaps in your checklist or execution flow
Emotional fog like fear, fatigue, or doubt
Time management or planning issues
These are things a win would have hidden.
4. Resets the Ego
Reminds you that success is earned every day through preparation, not luck or assumption.
Strips away entitlement and brings you back to grounded focus.
“I’m not owed success. I must earn it through discipline.”
5. Dissolves Outcome Attachment
Each missed trade is a chance to train your nervous system:
To trust your edge
To let go of "perfect" trades
To focus on consistency, not moments
“One trade does not define your career. Missing one doesn’t destroy your edge.”
6. Increases Long-Term Patience
Not reacting to a missed trade builds emotional control.
You prove you can protect your capital and stick to your edge—even when it hurts.
This is what consistency actually looks like.
7. Prepares You for Bigger Opportunities
Missing a trade now is training for bigger trades in the future.
The market will offer more—but only if you’ve built the poise to seize them with size.
You’re learning how to show up powerfully when it truly matters.
Final Reflection
Missed trades are not failures—they are feedback.
They train you to:
Stay calm without a win
Rebuild focus after discomfort
Show up sharp for the next opportunity
When you learn to detach from the fantasy of the “perfect trade,” you step into the role of the professional trader—patient, poised, and unshakeable.
 These answers were summarised with the help of PatGPT.

They are intended as a general guide. In upcoming modules, you'll learn how to identify and neutralise your specific psychological charges to create lasting transformation in your mindset and performance.
